events.title: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth while attending a performance of Our American Cousin at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C. He died the following morning, April 15.
events.significance: Lincoln's death, days after the Confederate surrender at Appomattox, was the first assassination of a U.S. president and profoundly shaped Reconstruction and the post-Civil War nation.

events.title: RMS Titanic Strikes an Iceberg
events.description: At 11:40 p.m. ship's time, the British ocean liner RMS Titanic struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic on her maiden voyage from Southampton to New York. She sank in the early hours of April 15, with more than 1,500 lives lost.
events.significance: The tragedy led to major reforms in maritime safety, including the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, requirements for sufficient lifeboats, and continuous radio watch.

events.title: Noah Webster Publishes the American Dictionary of the English Language
events.description: Noah Webster published his landmark two-volume dictionary containing about 70,000 entries, with distinctly American spellings and usages.
events.significance: The dictionary helped standardize American English and established the Webster name as a lasting authority on language.

events.title: Black Sunday Dust Storm
events.description: A massive dust storm swept across the Great Plains of the United States, carrying topsoil in huge black clouds over Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, and neighboring states during the Dust Bowl.
events.significance: Black Sunday became a symbol of the Dust Bowl disaster, drawing national attention to soil erosion and leading to federal soil conservation efforts.
